title: Scaleable streaming load harness for chat (SSE + WebSocket)
creator: Asha Raghavan
description: Purpose: build a production-representative, scalable load-testing harness that simulates streaming chat/completions over SSE and WebSocket, measures tokens/sec and p95 streaming latencies, and detects regressions automatically. The harness should be able to: 1) open O(10k) concurrent streaming connections, 2) support realistic conversation flows (multi-turn, role tokens, system + user + assistant deltas), 3) instrument token-level timestamps so we can compute tokens/sec and p95 token emission latency, 4) run scheduled nightly regression tests and optional gating checks on runtime changes. Design constraints: respect rate limits and simulate realistic client pacing (backpressure, reconnect/backoff), support both SSE and WebSocket endpoints, integrate with OpenTelemetry tracing and existing Grafana dashboards, and store raw traces/artifacts to S3 for offline analysis. Deliverables: reusable CLI and Kubernetes job templates, dashboards for tokens/sec and p95(stream-token-latency), alerting rules for regression thresholds, example workload configs per model family, and CI pipeline integration for nightly runs and per-PR smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can sustain 10k concurrent streaming connections across SSE and WebSocket in our staging Dedicated cluster without overwhelming control plane
Per-token timestamps are captured and both tokens/sec and p95 token emit latency are computed within 5% error vs synthetic ground truth
Nightly run publishes dashboard snapshot and creates a regression issue automatically when p95 increases by >15% vs 28-day baseline
Artifacts (Parquet traces, CSV summaries) are exported to s3://redwood-load-tests/streaming/ with retention policy and linked in test report
Runbooks for killing/isolating runs and cost caps documented and tested
runbook: Step 1: start harness controller (k8s job template available in //deploy/load-tests/streaming.yaml)
Step 2: load workload config (workloads/<model_family>.yaml) and override concurrency with --concurrency flag
Step 3: monitor grafana dashboard 'streaming-load/nightly' and 'runtime/tokens-per-sec' during run
Step 4: if stream_stall_rate > 1%, pause run, capture recent trace bundle and open ENG issue with tag load-test-failure
Step 5: to abort large runs set environment variable MAX_COST_USD and the controller will drain clients and stop new connections
